title: Tricksters and Friends
objectives: I can use clever, gentle, greedy, honest, polite, and patient to tell about a character.
I can tell why a character did something.
I can tell which words describe a good friend.
I can show with words and pictures how someone is honest or polite.
rationale: Characters in first-grade stories are often clever, greedy, or polite, and these words let children say why a character did what they did. They are grouped by what they tell us about a person: good friend words (gentle, honest, polite, patient) and thinking words (clever, greedy). The unit revisits lesson, unkind, and unfair, because first graders learn what makes a character unkind or unfair and what a story's lesson is when a character changes.

words.def: Good at thinking of smart ways to do things.
words.ex: The clever fox found a way to cross the stream.
words.ex2: It was clever of Dan to use a box as a drum.

apps.academic: The clever character solved the problem.
apps.writing: Tell how a clever character fixed a problem.

cloze.s: The ___ crow dropped stones in the jar to raise the water.

cloze2.s: Only a ___ child could solve that hard puzzle so fast.

misuse.s: The clever girl could not think of any ideas at all.
misuse.why: Clever means good at thinking of smart ways. A girl with no ideas is not clever.

visual.alt: A fox with a light bulb above its head.

words.ex: Use a gentle hand when you pet the kitten.
words.ex2: The gentle giant in the story never hurt anyone.

apps.academic: Be gentle with the class pet.
apps.writing: Tell how a gentle character acts.

cloze.s: Be ___ with the baby bird, because it is small and can be hurt.

cloze2.s: The ___ horse let the child pet its nose.

misuse.s: The gentle bear smashed the door down and growled at everyone.
misuse.why: Gentle means soft and kind. Smashing doors and growling is rough.

visual.alt: Two hands holding a rabbit softly.

words.def: Wanting much more than your share.
words.ex: The greedy dog ate all the treats.
words.ex2: The greedy king wanted every coin in the land.
words.nonExample: Sharing your snack is not greedy.

apps.academic: The greedy character took too much.
apps.writing: Tell what a greedy character took.

cloze.s: The ___ boy took all the cookies and left none for his sister.

cloze2.s: A ___ crow grabbed every coin and would not share.

misuse.s: The greedy girl gave away all her toys and kept nothing.
misuse.why: Greedy means wanting too much. Giving away everything is the opposite.

visual.alt: A child hugging a big pile of cookies.

words.def: Telling the truth and not cheating.
words.ex: An honest girl gave back the lost coin.
words.ex2: It is honest to say you broke the cup.

apps.academic: An honest answer tells what really happened.
apps.spoken: I will be honest with you.
apps.writing: Tell how an honest character told the truth.

cloze.s: The ___ boy told his mom the truth: he had spilled the milk.

cloze2.s: She found a wallet on the street and returned it, because she is ___.

misuse.s: The honest boy told a big lie so nobody would be mad.
misuse.why: Honest means telling the truth. Telling a lie is not honest.

visual.alt: A child handing a coin back to another child.

words.def: Showing good manners to other people.
words.ex: It is polite to say please and thank you.
words.ex2: The polite boy held the door for the next person.

apps.academic: Use polite words when you ask.
apps.writing: Tell how a polite character acts.

cloze.s: A ___ child says thank you when someone helps.

cloze2.s: Please wait your turn and be ___ to the people in line.

misuse.s: The polite girl grabbed the last cookie and shouted, "Mine!"
misuse.why: Polite means showing good manners. Grabbing and shouting is rude.

visual.alt: A smiling child holding a door open.

words.def: Able to wait calmly without getting upset.
words.ex: The patient cat sat by the hole for an hour.
words.ex2: Be patient while the cake bakes in the oven.

apps.academic: Be patient when you wait for your turn.
apps.writing: Tell how a patient character waits.

cloze.s: Growing a plant takes time, so you must be ___.

cloze2.s: The ___ fisherman waited all morning for a single fish.

misuse.s: The patient boy stomped and shouted because he had to wait one minute.
misuse.why: Patient means waiting calmly. Stomping and shouting is not patient.

visual.alt: An hourglass beside a small growing plant.

passage.title: Pip and the Cheese
paras: A greedy cat wanted all the cheese in the kitchen. Pip the mouse was clever, so he made a plan. He was polite and gentle when he asked the cat to share. He was patient and waited. Then the honest mouse said, "Sharing is more fun." The cat gave Pip half.

qs.q: Who was greedy in the story?
qs.why: The story says a greedy cat wanted all the cheese.

qs.q: How did Pip ask the cat to share?
choices: He did not ask at all.
He asked in a polite and gentle way.
qs.why: The story says Pip was polite and gentle when he asked the cat to share.

qs.q: What lesson does the story show?
choices: Sharing is better than being greedy.
qs.why: Pip's gentle, honest asking made the greedy cat share.

write.prompt: Draw a friend who is kind and polite. Say or write what your friend does.

study.task: Which of these words tell about a good friend? Which one tells about someone who does not share? Say why.

sentences: Say a sentence about someone who is polite.
Write a sentence about a clever animal.
Tell about a time you had to be patient.

given: The fox wanted all the grapes.
combine.model: The greedy fox wanted all the grapes and did not share.

given: She said she broke the cup.
combine.model: Lena was honest when she said she broke the cup.

discuss: Why is it good to be honest even when it is hard?
How can you be gentle with a pet?
produce.explain: Explain why a polite child says please. Use because.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a clever animal and a greedy animal in a story.
constructed.model: The clever mouse made a plan. The greedy cat wanted all the cheese.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a time someone was honest or patient.
constructed.model: My friend was honest and told the teacher the truth. I was patient while I waited for my turn.

teacher.overview: Children learn six words that tell what a character is like, then use them to describe characters in a short story. The unit revisits lesson, unkind, and unfair.

notes.va.clever.adj: Clever is good at thinking of smart ways. Use a puzzle or a trick from a story. Clever is not the same as sneaky; a clever character may be kind.
notes.va.gentle.adj: Pass a soft toy and say gentle hands. Link to the opposite rough, and to unkind from unit 8.
notes.va.greedy.adj: Greedy means wanting too much. Use a plate with too many cookies. Ask 'What would be a fair share?' Link to unfair.
notes.va.honest.adj: Honest means telling the truth. Role-play a small mistake and an honest answer. Avoid shaming a child who tells the truth.
notes.va.polite.adj: Polite is about good manners. Collect polite phrases (please, thank you, excuse me). Polite can look different at home and school.
notes.va.patient.adj: Patient is waiting calmly. Use a timer for a sand-clock wait. Note that the noun patient (a sick person) has a different meaning; teach only the describing sense.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The fox wants all the grapes. He takes every one and will not share, so he is greedy. The little bird thinks of a plan to get the grapes, so she is clever. She asks in a polite voice and waits, so she is patient. When she says what really happened, she is honest.'
discuss: Which character word would you like to be?
Why did the cat finally share?
extend: Children draw a character and write one character word under the picture.
Play 'Show Me': say a word and children freeze in a pose that shows it.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit greedy, honest, and polite the next day with a new story, again at one week, and use the words when children retell a story. They return in grade 2 with richer character words.

wida.oral: Partner A acts out a character without speaking. Partner B names the character word and says why.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (astuto, gentil, codicioso, honesto, educado, paciente) are not reviewed by a native speaker; gentle may be amable or suave, and polite may be cortés.
Patient also means a person at a doctor's office; only the describing sense is taught.
The ladder (unkind, rude, polite, gentle) is informal and includes rude, which is not a unit word.
